- When sentiment is strongly positive (≥ 0.67) in recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast slightly to align with mean reversion.
- When sentiment is negative (≤ 0.00) or volatile, model often underestimates; increase forecast modestly to account for risk aversion or market correction.
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., >75.0), model frequently overcorrects downward; cap downward revisions to avoid excessive lag.
- Model consistently underestimates early in the 30-day horizon (first 5–7 days) when sentiment is neutral or slightly positive; adjust upward by 1–2% for first 5 days.
- If sentiment turns negative mid-horizon, model often fails to adjust quickly; apply a “sentiment decay” rule: reduce forecast by 0.5–1.0% per day for negative sentiment.
- Model shows persistent bias toward higher prices when sentiment is clustered near 0.67–0.70; apply a “sentiment ceiling” rule: cap forecast at 10% above recent 7-day average if sentiment > 0.65.
- For long-term (last 10+ days) forecasts, model tends to underestimate; apply a “mean reversion buffer” rule: add 0.5–1.0% to forecast if recent 7-day average is > 72.0.
